\section{Representable presheaves are fppf sheaves}\label{sec:representable-fppf}


We now deduce from fppf descent for quasi-coherent sheaves that every scheme defines a sheaf for the fppf topology, and hence for all topologies of Definition~\ref{def:standard-sites}. The argument has three steps:
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The fully faithful part of Theorem~\ref{thm:fppf-descent-qcoh}, applied to the structure sheaf, shows that $T\mapsto\Gamma(T,\mathcal{O}_T)$ satisfies fppf descent.
	\item Morphisms into an affine scheme $\Specof{A}$ are ring maps out of $A$, and the representable preshef $\Hom_{\Ring}(A,-)$ preserves limits. This gives the case of affine targets without any computation.
	\item For an arbitrary target we descend open subsets along the covering and reduce to (2).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:structure-sheaf-fppf}
	Let $p:U\to T$ be an fppf covering of schemes. Then
	\[
	\begin{tikzcd}
		\Gamma(T,\mathcal{O}_T) \arrow[r, "p^*"] & \Gamma(U,\mathcal{O}_U) \arrow[r, shift left, "\mathrm{pr}_0^*"] \arrow[r, shift right, "\mathrm{pr}_1^*"'] & \Gamma(U\times_TU,\mathcal{O}_{U\times_TU})
	\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	is an equalizer diagram of rings.
\end{corollary}





\begin{proof}
	By Theorem~\ref{thm:fppf-descent-qcoh}, the functor
	\[
	D:\QCoh(T)\longrightarrow\Desc(U/T),
	\qquad
	\mathcal F\longmapsto
	(p^*\mathcal F,\mathrm{can}_{\mathcal F})
	\]
	of Definition~\ref{con:pullback-to-descent}
	is fully faithful. In particular, it induces a bijection
	\[
		\Hom_{\QCoh(T)}(\mathcal O_T,\mathcal O_T)
		\xrightarrow{\sim}
		\Hom_{\Desc(U/T)}
		\bigl(D(\mathcal O_T),D(\mathcal O_T)\bigr)
	\]
	For every scheme $V$, evaluation at $1$ gives a canonical
	bijection
	\[
	\Hom_{\QCoh(V)}(\mathcal O_V,\mathcal O_V)
	\xrightarrow{\sim}
	\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V),
	\]
	whose inverse sends a section $t$ to multiplication by $t$,
	denoted $m_t$, see \cite[][Tag 01AL]{stacks-project}.
	
	
	Write
	\[
	\varepsilon:p^*\mathcal{O}_T\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathcal{O}_U
	\]
	for the canonical isomorphism $p^\sharp$. For $i=0,1$, let
	\[
	\lambda_i:
	\mathrm{pr}_i^*p^*\mathcal O_T
	\xrightarrow{\sim}
	(p\circ \mathrm{pr}_i)^*\mathcal O_T
	\xrightarrow{\sim}
	\mathcal O_{U\times_T U}
	\]
	be the canonical composite.
	
	Since $p\circ \mathrm{pr}_0=p\circ \mathrm{pr}_1$, the definition of the
	canonical descent isomorphism gives
	\[
	\lambda_1 \circ\mathrm{can}_{\mathcal O_T}
	=\lambda_0.
	\]
	Thus the following diagram commutes:
	% https://q.uiver.app/#
	\[\begin{tikzcd}
		{\mathrm{pr}_0^*p^*\mathcal O_T} & {\mathrm{pr}_1^*p^*\mathcal O_T} \\
		{\mathcal{O}_{U\times_T U}} & {\mathcal{O}_{U\times_T U}}
		\arrow["{\mathrm{can}_{\mathcal{O}_T}}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
		\arrow["{\lambda_0}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
		\arrow["{\lambda_1}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{id}}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\end{tikzcd}\]
	
	Now let $s\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal{O}_U)$, such that
	$\mathrm{pr}_0^*s = \mathrm{pr}_1^*s \in \Gamma(U\times_T U,\mathcal{O}_{U\times_T U})$. Define
	\[
	b:=\varepsilon^{-1}\circ m_s\circ\varepsilon:
	p^*\mathcal O_T\longrightarrow p^*\mathcal O_T.
	\]
	We claim that $b$ is a morphism of descent data.
	Hence, we need to show that
	\[
	(\mathrm{pr}_1^*b)\circ\mathrm{can}_{\mathcal O_T}
	=
	\mathrm{can}_{\mathcal O_T}\circ(\mathrm{pr}_0^*b).
	\]
	
	Under the isomorphisms $\lambda_i$, the endomorphism
	$\mathrm{pr}_i^*b$ becomes multiplication by $\mathrm{pr}_i^*s$.i.e. the following diagramm commutes:
	% https://q.uiver.app/#
	\[\begin{tikzcd}
		{\mathrm{pr}_i^*p^*\mathcal{O}_T} & {\mathrm{pr}_i^*p^*\mathcal{O}_T} \\
		{\mathrm{pr}_i^*\mathcal{O}_U} & {\mathrm{pr}_i^*\mathcal{O}_U} \\
		{\mathcal{O}_{U\times_TU}} & {\mathcal{O}_{U\times_TU}}
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_i^*b}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_i^*\varepsilon}", from=1-1, to=2-1]
		\arrow["{\lambda_i}"', bend right=40, from=1-1, to=3-1]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_i^*\varepsilon}"', from=1-2, to=2-2]
		\arrow["{\lambda_i}", bend left=40, from=1-2, to=3-2]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_i^*m_s}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
		\arrow["\cong", from=2-1, to=3-1]
		\arrow["\cong"', from=2-2, to=3-2]
		\arrow["{m_{\mathrm{pr}_i^*s}}"', from=3-1, to=3-2]
	\end{tikzcd}\]
	
	
	Now this fits into the the following diagram:
	% https://q.uiver.app/#
	\[\begin{tikzcd}
		{\mathcal{O}_{U\times_TU}} &&&&& {\mathcal{O}_{U\times_TU}} \\
		& {\mathrm{pr}_0^*\mathcal{O}_U} &&& {\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal{O}_U} \\
		&& {\mathrm{pr}_0^*p^*\mathcal{O}_T} & {\mathrm{pr}_1^*p^*\mathcal{O}_T} \\
		&& {\mathrm{pr}_0^*p^*\mathcal{O}_T} & {\mathrm{pr}_1^*p^*\mathcal{O}_T} \\
		& {\mathrm{pr}_0^*\mathcal{O}_U} &&& {\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal{O}_U} \\
		{\mathcal{O}_{U\times_TU}} &&&&& {\mathcal{O}_{U\times_TU}}
		\arrow["{\mathrm{id}}", from=1-1, to=1-6]
		\arrow["{m_{\mathrm{pr}_0^*s}}"', from=1-1, to=6-1]
		\arrow["{m_{\mathrm{pr}_1^*s}}", from=1-6, to=6-6]
		\arrow["\cong", from=2-2, to=1-1]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_0^*m_s}"', from=2-2, to=5-2]
		\arrow[from=2-5, to=1-6]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_1^*m_s}", from=2-5, to=5-5]
		\arrow["{\lambda_0}"', bend right=25, from=3-3, to=1-1]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_0^*\varepsilon}", from=3-3, to=2-2]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{can}_{\mathcal O_T}}"', from=3-3, to=3-4]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_0^*b}"', from=3-3, to=4-3]
		\arrow["{\lambda_1}", bend left=25, from=3-4, to=1-6]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_0^*\varepsilon}"', from=3-4, to=2-5]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_1^*b}", from=3-4, to=4-4]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{can}_{\mathcal O_T}}"', from=4-3, to=4-4]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_0^*\varepsilon}"', from=4-3, to=5-2]
		\arrow["{\lambda_0}", bend left=25, from=4-3, to=6-1]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_0^*\varepsilon}", from=4-4, to=5-5]
		\arrow["{\lambda_1}"', bend right=25, from=4-4, to=6-6]
		\arrow["\cong"', from=5-2, to=6-1]
		\arrow[from=5-5, to=6-6]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{id}}"', from=6-1, to=6-6]
	\end{tikzcd}\]
	
	By assumption, $\mathrm{pr}_0^*s = \mathrm{pr}_1^*s$, hence, the outter square commutes and so does the inner square, so $b$ is inceed a morphism of descent data.
	
	
	
	
	
	By full faithfulness of $D$, there is a unique
	$\mathcal O_T$-linear endomorphism
	$a:\mathcal O_T\to\mathcal O_T$ such that $p^*a=b$.
	Write $a=m_t$ for the corresponding section
	$t\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Then
	\[
	m_s
	=\varepsilon\circ b\circ\varepsilon^{-1}
	=\varepsilon\circ p^*m_t\circ\varepsilon^{-1}
	=m_{p^*t}.
	\]
	Evaluating at $1$ yields $s=p^*t$.
	
	If $t'\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ also satisfies
	$p^*t'=s$, then
	\[
	p^*m_{t'}
	=\varepsilon^{-1}\circ m_s\circ\varepsilon
	=b.
	\]
	By the uniqueness of $a$, we obtain $m_{t'}=m_t$,
	hence $t'=t$.
	
	Finally, every section pulled back from $T$ satisfies
	$\mathrm{pr}_0^*p^*t=\mathrm{pr}_1^*p^*t$, since $p\circ \mathrm{pr}_0=p\circ \mathrm{pr}_1$.
	Therefore $p^*$ identifies $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$
	bijectively with the subring
	\[
	\{s\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)
	\mid \mathrm{pr}_0^*s=\mathrm{pr}_1^*s\}.
	\]
	As $p^*$ is a ring homomorphism, this identification
	is an isomorphism of rings. Thus the asserted diagram
	is an equalizer of rings.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:representable-affine-target}
	Let $X=\Specof{A}$ be an affine scheme and let $p:U\to T$ be an fppf covering. Then $h_X$ satisfies descent along $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
	By the adjunction $\Gamma \dashv \Spec$ for every scheme $T$, the is a natural isomorphism
	\begin{align*}
			\Hom_{\Sch}(T,\Specof{A}) & \to\Hom_{\Ring}(A,\Gamma(T,\mathcal{O}_T)) \\
				 f &\mapsto f^\sharp,
	\end{align*} see (\cite[][Tag 01I1]{stacks-project}). Hence there is a natural isomorphism of presheaves
	\[
	h_X\cong\Hom_{\Ring}(A,-)\circ\Gamma(-, \mathcal{O}_{(-)}).
	\]
	The representable functor $\Hom_{\Ring}(A,-):\Ring\to\Set$ preserves all limits, in particular equalizers and by the adjunction $\Gamma \dashv \Spec$, $\Gamma$ preserves all limites. Hence, applying $\Hom_{\Ring}(A, - )$ to the equalizer of Corollary \ref{cor:structure-sheaf-fppf} shows that
	\[
	h_X(T)\longrightarrow h_X(U)\rightrightarrows h_X(U\times_TU)
	\]
	is an equalizer, which means that $h_X$ satisfies descent along $p$ by Proposition \ref{prop:cech-descent-equalizer}.
\end{proof}

For a general target, the only additional input is that open subsets descend along fppf coverings.


\begin{theorem}\label{thm:representable-fppf-sheaf}
	(\cite[][Tag 023Q]{stacks-project}, \cite[][Theorem~2.55]{vistoli2007notes})
	Let $X$ be a scheme. Then the representable presheaf $h_X=\Hom_\Sch(-,X)$ satisfies the sheaf condition for every fppf covering. In particular, $h_X$ is a sheaf on $\Sch_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski}, \text{\etale}, \mathrm{fppf}\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
	Morphisms of schemes glue uniquely along open coverings.
	By Corollary~\ref{cor:sheaf-via-cech}, it therefore suffices
	to prove that, for every fppf covering $p:U\to T$, the diagram
	\[
	\Hom(T,X)\longrightarrow \Hom(U,X)
	\rightrightarrows \Hom(U\times_T U,X)
	\]
	is an equalizer. Write
	$\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2:U\times_T U\rightrightarrows U$
	for the projections, and choose an affine open covering
	$X=\bigcup_{i\in I}X_i$.
	
	\emph{Uniqueness.}
	Let $g,g':T\to X$ satisfy $g\circ p=g'\circ p$.
	Since $p$ is surjective, the equality
	\[
	p^{-1}\bigl(g^{-1}(X_i)\bigr)
	=
	p^{-1}\bigl(g'^{-1}(X_i)\bigr)
	\]
	implies
	\[
	T_i:=g^{-1}(X_i)=g'^{-1}(X_i).
	\]
	Hence, the restrictions $g|_{T_i},g'|_{T_i}:T_i\to X_i$ agree
	after pullback along the fppf covering $p^{-1}(T_i)\to T_i$. Since $X_i$ are assumed to be affine, $g|_{T_i}$ and $g'|_{T_i}$ are equal by
	Lemma~\ref{lem:representable-affine-target}.
	As the $T_i$ cover $T$, we obtain $g=g'$.
	
	\emph{Existence.}
	Let $f:U\to X$ be a morphism such that
	\begin{align}\label{eq:compability-condition}
		f\circ\mathrm{pr}_1=f\circ\mathrm{pr}_2.
	\end{align}
	Write $\iota_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ for the inclusions.
	Set $U_i:=f^{-1}(X_i)$. Then
	\[
	\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(U_i)
	=
	(f\circ\mathrm{pr}_1)^{-1}(X_i)
	=
	(f\circ\mathrm{pr}_2)^{-1}(X_i)
	=
	\mathrm{pr}_2^{-1}(U_i).
	\]
	
	Set $T_i = p(U_i)$. Since $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation,
	it is open by \cite[][Tag 01UA]{stacks-project}. Thus each $T_i$ is open in $T$.
	We claim that $p^{-1}(T_i)=U_i$.
	The inclusion $U_i\subseteq p^{-1}(T_i)$ is obvious.
	By construction, $U_i\to T_i$ is surjective.
	Its base change
	\[
	q:p^{-1}(T_i)\times_{T_i}U_i
	\longrightarrow p^{-1}(T_i)
	\]
	is therefore surjective
	(\cite[][Tag 01S1]{stacks-project}).
	Under the canonical identification
	\[
	p^{-1}(T_i)\times_{T_i}U_i
	\cong U\times_T U_i,
	\]
	the morphism $q$ is induced by the first projection.
	On $U\times_T U_i$, the compatibility condition gives
	\[
	f\circ\mathrm{pr}_0=f\circ\mathrm{pr}_1.
	\]
	Since the second projection factors through $U_i$,
	the right-hand side factors through $X_i$.
	Consequently, the first projection factors through
	$f^{-1}(X_i)=U_i$.
	Thus $q$ factors through the open immersion
	\[
	U_i\hookrightarrow p^{-1}(T_i).
	\]
	Surjectivity of $q$ implies that this open immersion
	is surjective, hence an isomorphism.
	Therefore $p^{-1}(T_i)=U_i$.
	
	
	
	
	Hence, the following diagram is cartesian and $p_i:U_i\to T_i$ is an fppf covering:
	% https://q.uiver.app/#
	\[\begin{tikzcd}
		{U_i} & {T_i} \\
		U & T
		\arrow["{p_i}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
		\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
		\arrow["\ulcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
		\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]
		\arrow["p"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\end{tikzcd}\]
	Moreover, the $T_i$ cover $T$, since for every $t\in T$, surjectivity of $p$ gives a point $u\in U$ over $t$, and $u\in U_i$ for some $i$, i.e. $t\in T_i$.
	
	Write $f_i:U_i\to X_i$ for the factorization of $f|_{U_i}$
	through $X_i$:
	% https://q.uiver.app/#
	\[\begin{tikzcd}
		{U_i} & {X_i} \\
		U & X
		\arrow["{f_i}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
		\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
		\arrow["\ulcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
		\arrow["{\iota_i}", hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]
		\arrow["f"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\end{tikzcd}\]
	
	Since $U_i=U\times_T T_i$, there is a canonical
	identification
	\[
	U_i\times_{T_i}U_i
	\cong (U\times_T U)\times_T T_i,
	\]
	and hence the following diagram commutes:
	% https://q.uiver.app/#
	\[\begin{tikzcd}
		{U_i\times_{T_i}U_i} & {U_i} & {T_i} \\
		{U\times_T U} & U & T
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_1}", shift left, from=1-1, to=1-2]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_2}"', shift right, from=1-1, to=1-2]
		\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
		\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-3]
		\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]
		\arrow[from=1-3, to=2-3]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_1}", shift left, from=2-1, to=2-2]
		\arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_2}"', shift right, from=2-1, to=2-2]
		\arrow["p"', from=2-2, to=2-3]
	\end{tikzcd}\]
	
	Restricting the compatibility condition (\ref{eq:compability-condition}) for $f$ along $U_i \hookrightarrow U$ therefore gives
	\[
	\iota_i\circ f_i\circ \mathrm{pr}_1 = f_{\mid U_i} \circ \mathrm{pr}_1
	= f_{\mid U_i} \circ \mathrm{pr}_2
	= \iota_i\circ f_i\circ \mathrm{pr}_2.
	\]
	As $\iota_i$ is a monomorphism, this implies
	\[
	f_i\circ \mathrm{pr}_1=f_i\circ \mathrm{pr}_2.
	\]
	Since $X_i$ is affine,
	Lemma~\ref{lem:representable-affine-target} yields a unique
	morphism $g_i:T_i\to X_i$ such that
	\[
	g_i\circ p_i=f_i.
	\]
	
	This all fits into the following commutative diagram:
	
	\begin{equation}\label{diag:representable-sheaf-zariski-descent}
		% https://q.uiver.app/#
		\begin{tikzcd}
			&&& {T_i} \\
			{U_i\times_{T_i}U_i} & {U_i} & {X_i} & T \\
			{U\times_T U} & U & X
			\arrow["{g_i}", dashed, from=1-4, to=2-3]
			\arrow[hook, from=1-4, to=2-4]
			\arrow["{pr_2}"', shift right, from=2-1, to=2-2]
			\arrow["{pr_1}", shift left, from=2-1, to=2-2]
			\arrow[from=2-1, to=3-1]
			\arrow["{p_i}", from=2-2, to=1-4]
			\arrow["{f_i}"', from=2-2, to=2-3]
			\arrow[hook, from=2-2, to=3-2]
			\arrow["{\iota_i}"{pos=0.7}, hook, from=2-3, to=3-3]
			\arrow["g", dashed, from=2-4, to=3-3]
			\arrow["{pr_1}", shift left, from=3-1, to=3-2]
			\arrow["{pr_2}"', shift right, from=3-1, to=3-2]
			\arrow["p"{pos=0.8}, from=3-2, to=2-4]
			\arrow["f"', from=3-2, to=3-3]
		\end{tikzcd}
	\end{equation}
	
	We now verify that the morphisms
	\[
	\widetilde g_i:=\iota_i\circ g_i:T_i\to X
	\]
	agree on overlaps to glue them to the morphism $g: T\to X$ fitting into diagram \ref{diag:representable-sheaf-zariski-descent} by Zariski descent.
	For $i,j\in I$, let
	\[
	T_{ij}:=T_i\cap T_j,
	\qquad
	U_{ij}:=p^{-1}(T_{ij})=U_i\cap U_j.
	\]
	The morphism $p_{ij}:U_{ij}\to T_{ij}$ induced by $p$
	is again an fppf covering.
	By construction,
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		\bigl(\widetilde g_i|_{T_{ij}}\bigr)\circ p_{ij}
		&=f|_{U_{ij}},\\
		\bigl(\widetilde g_j|_{T_{ij}}\bigr)\circ p_{ij}
		&=f|_{U_{ij}}.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	By uniqueness, applied to
	$p_{ij}:U_{ij}\to T_{ij}$, implies
	\[
	\widetilde g_i|_{T_{ij}}
	=
	\widetilde g_j|_{T_{ij}}.
	\]
	Hence the $\widetilde g_i$ glue to a morphism $g:T\to X$ by Zariski descent, since $\{T_i\subset T\}_{i\in I}$ is an open covering.
	
	Finally, on every $U_i$ we have
	\[
	(g\circ p)|_{U_i}
	=
	\widetilde g_i\circ p_i
	=
	\iota_i\circ f_i
	=
	f|_{U_i}.
	\]
	Since the $U_i$ cover $U$, it follows that $g\circ p=f$.
\end{proof}


\begin{corollary}[Relative version]\label{cor:representable-relative}
	Let $S$ be a scheme,\\
	$\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski}, \text{\etale}, \mathrm{fppf}\}$, and $X$ a scheme over $S$. Then $h_{X/S}=\Hom_S(-,X)$ is a sheaf on $(\SchOver{S})_\tau$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
	Let $\{U_i\to T\}$ be a $\tau$-covering in $\SchOver{S}$ and let $f_i:U_i\to X$ be $S$-morphisms that agree on all $U_i\times_TU_j$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:representable-fppf-sheaf} they glue uniquely to a morphism $f:T\to X$. Composing with the structure morphism $X\to S$, the two morphisms $T\to S$ given by $X\to S$ composed with $f$ and by the structure morphism of $T$ agree on every $U_i$, so they are equal by injectivity in Theorem~\ref{thm:representable-fppf-sheaf} applied to $h_S$. Hence $f$ is an $S$-morphism.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
	Theorem~\ref{thm:representable-fppf-sheaf} says that the sites $\Sch_\tau$ and $(\SchOver{S})_\tau$ are subcanonical. By the Yoneda lemma, $X\mapsto h_X$ is a fully faithful functor $\SchOver{S}\to\Sh{(\SchOver{S})_{\mathrm{fppf}}}$. This is the starting point of the chapter on algebraic spaces, where algebraic spaces are defined as fppf sheaves that are \etale\ locally representable.
\end{remark}
